name: The Priest's House

dates.note: THE ENTRY DOES STATE 1308 AND A FIRST PASS OF THIS RECORD SAID IT DID NOT. The Details section's closing paragraph, returned only by a second extract with a different query, reads 'the house first mentioned 1308, said to be "ruinous' in 1608' -- which is exactly the year the node's exemplar carries and exactly the sense in which the node carries it ('First recorded in 1308'). The entry's own dating of the FABRIC remains 'C14 and later', with features dated late C15, possibly C14 and probably C17. One extract returns one span, and reporting 'the entry does not say' after one query is the error this layer keeps meeting.

refs.title: The Priest's House, Muchelney - Wikipedia
refs.note: THE ONLY OVERALL DIMENSION ANY SOURCE IN THIS CLUSTER STATES, and it is here rather than in `measurements` because `measurements[]` indexes `survey.quotes[]` and the survey block is the list entry, which states no dimension. Read as continuous prose in an extract: 'The two-storey thatched hall house is made of local stone with hamstone dressings. Externally the house measures 51 feet (16 m) by 22 feet (6.7 m) wide. It has four bays along the south front which incorporates original Gothic doorway and tracery windows.' The four bays and the two storeys agree with the list entry exactly; the 51 by 22 ft is uncorroborated here and carries no citation on the Wikipedia page as extracted.

quotes.text: Bay 1 has 3-light chamfered mullioned windows, possibly C19, with flat heads, and square labels; bay 2 has moulded pointed arched doorway with arched label, old boarded and studded door, with covermoulds to joints; bay 3 has a 4-light full-height mullioned and transomed solar type window, with 4-centre arched lights below transome and cinquefoil cusped lights above, with quatrefoils in tracery, late C15 probably, all under square label

quotes.text: mullioned window with 4-centre arched lights having some early external ferramenta, under square label; above a small 2-light window with trefoil cusped lights and incised spandrils, possibly C14, this last cut into thatch: all windows leaded, bay 1 with rectangular panes, the remainder with diamond panes.

quotes.text: The original form and subsequent alteration of house much discussed: the house first mentioned 1308, said to be "ruinous' in 1608; it was used by the vicar or curate until c1840, when the house was used as a cellar and later as a school, and in late C19 was rented by a farmer. Acquired by the National Trust in 1911.

note: Tranche 3, the English cottage and the Cotswold vernacular, 5 Sep 2026. The list entry states no dimension; a Wikipedia sentence does, and it is carried in that reference's note rather than in `measurements` because the survey block admits one source and this record's is the list entry. The entry independently confirms the two details the node's exemplar note already claimed -- lias stone with Ham stone dressings, and a thatched roof 'with stepped coped gable to west, half hipped to east' -- and adds the window cut into the thatch. A QUOTE THAT STRADDLED TWO EXTRACT CHUNKS WAS FOUND BY RE-EXTRACTING THE PAGE WITH A DIFFERENT QUERY AND WAS SPLIT RATHER THAN JOINED. The chunker returns the same boundaries on every query and each block repeats the tail of the one before, so the text is demonstrably continuous -- but a span crossing the boundary was never READ as one contiguous run, and this record does not print one as though it had been.
